verified.exploit_entry_point: The plugin management operations of pkg/plugin.Manager, reached from the `trivy plugin` CLI subcommands (install, uninstall, refresh, prefetch) and from the package's public Go API. Tests drive the real Manager methods (NewManager().Install/Uninstall/Refresh/Prefetch) with XDG_DATA_HOME pointed at a temp dir, exactly as the project's own pkg/plugin tests do; nothing is stubbed. The attacker input is a plugin name carried in a plugin's packaged metadata, in stored on-disk metadata, in a CLI argument, or in an index entry.
variants: base (published fix, pattern A): a plugin's packaged metadata declares a name containing '..'; the install destination is the name joined onto the plugin root, so the downloader clears and writes, and the metadata copy is written, outside the plugin root (CVE write/delete sink).
far site (published fix, pattern A): the uninstall command joins its CLI name argument onto the plugin root and RemoveAll's it, so a '..' name deletes a directory outside the plugin root.

injected sibling (reload / stored-name path): an installed plugin's stored metadata name is joined onto the plugin root to form its directory; a maintenance operation that writes into that directory escapes the root when the stored name contains '..'. Reason to dismiss: the metadata was written by Trivy itself at install time, so it reads as trusted.

injected sibling (index/prefetch path): a cache directory is reserved for a plugin by joining an index-entry name onto the plugin root; a '..' name creates a directory outside the root. Reason to dismiss: the name identifies an entry in Trivy's curated plugin index, which reads as trusted.
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own pkg/plugin suite (manager_test.go, manager_unix_test.go, index_test.go) builds and passes at the pinned+injected commit and on the oracle (go test ./pkg/plugin/ with GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.3 GOEXPERIMENT=jsonv2). The pinned commit does not contain the advisory's regression tests (testdata/escaping_name, testdata/absolute_name and the escaping-name subtests are added only by the fix commit). The functional suite re-runs the deterministic subset (Uninstall, Information, LoadAll, Run) plus the task's own legitimate-use tests; the install suite (which drives an httptest git server) is exercised at build time only. Hidden suites: 4 security tests fail on pinned+injected and pass on the oracle; 13 functional cases pass on both.

traps.shape: the published fix's protected sink: a plugin name from packaged metadata is joined onto the plugin root to form the install destination, which is cleared and written
traps.where: pkg/plugin/manager.go:129 (loadMetadata) and manager.go:139 (destination write), reached from Manager.install
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none needed - this is the write the advisory title points at; the obvious lever

traps.shape: a far site the published fix also protects: the uninstall path joins a CLI name argument onto the plugin root and removes it
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the name is the local user's own command-line argument, so it reads as trusted input rather than attacker-controlled

traps.shape: save/reload sibling: an installed plugin's directory is derived from the name stored in its on-disk metadata; a maintenance operation that writes into that directory escapes the root when the stored name contains '..'
traps.where: pkg/plugin/manager.go loadMetadata (plugin.dir derived from stored name) + injected Manager.Refresh (added by inject.patch)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the stored metadata was written by Trivy itself during install, so its recorded name reads as trusted; a fix placed on the install argument alone leaves this reload path open
traps.realistic_because: the stored-name-to-directory derivation is real unmodified pinned code; the maintenance operation that writes via it is injected into our copy only in the same lookup-then-use style as the surrounding methods; registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

traps.shape: index/accessor sibling: a cache directory is reserved for a plugin by joining an index-entry name onto the plugin root
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the name identifies an entry in Trivy's curated plugin index, which reads as trusted, and the operation only reserves a cache directory
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer adding a prefetch/cache convenience keyed by the index name would reuse the same name-joined-onto-root pattern as the existing methods; INJECTED into our copy only, registered in build/audit/uncovered-routes.tsv

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security tests assert no out-of-root side effect and ignore the error; a panic or crash fails the test (the test goroutine aborts) rather than being scored as a pass, so a crash cannot pass as a refusal
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is a single protected resource - the plugin root directory - and no neighbouring or proxy resource that a fix could authorize by mistake
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: path traversal here is one-way and role-free; there are no peers, roles or directions of which a fix could cover only one
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the correct guard tests the raw name before any join or clean; there is no normalizing/adjusting step applied to the attacker value ahead of the check that a fix could be fooled by
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the name is validated structurally (is it a plain local path) and compared by path semantics; no identity string is parsed into fields where a malformed spelling could slip past
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: confinement is structural, decided from the name and the fixed plugin root; there is no external authority that could return empty and make the check fail open
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the fix is applied per call site inside the plugin package; it does not retune a shared helper whose contract a sibling API depends on (hardening.patch adds defence in depth without changing any API's stated behaviour)

notes: Injected track. inject.patch (in environment/) adds two maintenance operations (a refresh and an index-prefetch helper) to our copy only, applied at image build after checkout. Oracle = signature-stable confinement (filepath.IsLocal at the install destination, the uninstall argument, the load argument and the prefetch name; the installed directory derived from the directory read rather than the stored name) closing base, the uninstall far site, and both injected siblings. The upstream fix uses an os.Root-based API with a changed NewManager signature; the oracle keeps the signature so the project's own pkg/plugin tests compile and pass unchanged. The upstream exec-path route (Platform.Bin joined onto the plugin dir, pkg/plugin/plugin.go:69) is a different field and sink (code the plugin author already controls); investigated and left out as the screener recommended; noted in uncovered-routes.tsv.
